study: Can one constant replace the final-filter table? Value of per-setting filter strength.
upstream_definition: Pre-filter estimate g_pre per channel and fit = the estimate the frozen receiver passes to its final filter: adaptive output (SNR <= 20 dB); start + EM tail (SNR > 20 dB); if the recovery check accepted an alternative, that alternative (unfiltered, since the table filter is off at reference key 5). Recovery trigger/acceptance decisions are those of the frozen receiver and are not recomputed per arm. See POLICY_TRACE.md.

arms.A: Current table: shrink.apply(g_pre, c_table, beta=1) where the table filters and the receiver calls finish; identity elsewhere. Must equal frozen gated() output with max abs diff exactly 0 on every validation and test cell, fit and channel; otherwise the study stops.
arms.C1: Noise scale, one global c, beta=1, applied in ALL settings (including SNR <= 20 dB).
arms.C2: Noise scale, one global c, beta=1, applied only on the high-SNR route (nominal SNR > 30 dB + 1e-10, the global-start/EM-tail path). This region contains every setting the table filters; the difference (RSR key 5 above 30 dB, and 31.25 dB at all references) is reported.
arms.D: Posterior scale: tau_k = c sqrt(2 u_k max(m,q)), u_k = user_uncertainty(Z, g_pre S + B, S, v) from uncertainty_vendored.py (byte copy of audit/uncertainty-filter-correction f1155f0b experiments/uncertainty_filter/uncertainty.py, sha256 54de64e3...e1a4); same smooth Hankel shrinkage, beta=1, all settings. Run only if the D gate passes.
arms.O: Oracle: per test cell (SNR x RSR x paths), the noise-scale c from the grid minimizing that cell's 3-fit mean test NMSE (dB), chosen with the true channel on the test draws (in-sample; optimistic by construction). Diagnostic only; never used to select A-D.

grid.posterior_c: noise_c values union sqrt(2) * noise_c values (22 values, c=0 once)

settings.test_cells: 153 grid + 45 (off-grid SNR x grid RSR x paths) + 132 (RSR 8,16 x 22 SNRs x paths) + 66 (RSR 0 x 22 SNRs x paths) = 396
settings.anchors: Per (regime, reference) block: 128 channels shared across all SNRs of that block (existing risk_data.make_anchor convention: one unit-noise realization scaled per SNR); 39 pilots = 30 fitting + 9 held-out.
settings.physical_seed: 1000 * role_seed + round(10 * RSR_dB) (existing formula, extended to RSR 0/8/16)

selection.data: validation draws only (153 grid cells); never test draws, never truth
selection.score: held-out exact Rician NLL (tcom_pilot_em_20261018.continuation.nll) of g S_h + B_h against the 9 held-out magnitudes, mean over entries; cell score = mean over 128 channels and 3 fits; objective = equal-cell mean over the 153 cells
selection.rule: argmin over the arm's grid; ties within 1e-12 -> smaller c
selection.diagnostic: also report the c that validation true-channel NMSE (equal-cell mean dB) would pick; not used
selection.d_gate: Run D only if, at the frozen C1 and C2 constants, C1's equal-cell mean held-out NLL over validation cells with SNR <= 30 dB is lower than C2's (= no filter there) by more than 1e-12. Otherwise record D as skipped: above 20 dB u_k equals the noise scale / sqrt(2) to within 0.3%, so D adds nothing where the filter acts.
selection.freeze: configs/frozen_choices.json with all selected constants, the D decision and validation bank hashes; its sha256 is written to configs/frozen_choices.sha256 and checked before any test draw is generated

metrics.cell_nmse_db: 10 log10(sum_channels ||G_hat - G||^2 / sum_channels ||G||^2) per fit, averaged over the 3 fits (existing reports)
metrics.mean_setting_nmse_db: equal-cell mean of cell NMSE dB over a scope
metrics.pooled_nmse: ratio of sums over all channels in a scope, per fit, mean over fits (linear and dB)
metrics.ber: existing exact 64-hypothesis Rician magnitude ML detector (tcom_followups_20261017/ber_detector.py), 64 Gray-QPSK vectors per channel, fresh data noise SeedSequence([ber_data, regime_index, round(10*RSR), local_index]) shared across SNR and arms; cell BER = mean over channels and fits
metrics.bootstrap: 20,000 multinomial resamples of the 128 anchors independently within each (regime, reference) block, shared across SNR, arm and fit (existing procedure); intervals for arm - A
metrics.runtime: complete call per arm (receiver + recovery check + arm filter, including u_k for D), one CPU thread, float64, randomized order, warm-up excluded; two windows (before and after the test accuracy runs) of 459 worlds (153 grid settings x 3 indices); p90 and max; scopes: full grid and target range (RSR 5, SNR > 30 dB, existing 'weak_target')

acceptance_limits.scope: 153-setting test grid. Off-grid and RSR 0 points get the same per-setting checks, reported as secondary (not part of pass/fail).
acceptance_limits.L1: mean-setting NMSE(arm) - NMSE(A) <= 0.3 dB over the full grid AND over 30-60 dB (SNR >= 30, 81 cells)
acceptance_limits.L2: no setting with NMSE(arm) - NMSE(A) > 1.0 dB
acceptance_limits.L3: no setting whose 95% bootstrap interval for BER(arm) - BER(A) lies entirely above zero
acceptance_limits.L4: p90 runtime <= 10.74 ms in the full grid and in the target range, in both windows
acceptance_limits.L4_contingency: This machine is not the Apple M2 on which 10.74 ms was set. If arm A itself fails the absolute cap here, L4 is reported as not assessable as written and the pre-registered substitute is used: arm p90 <= 1.02 x A p90 in both scopes and both windows. The user is told.
acceptance_limits.preference: If several arms pass, prefer C1, then C2, then D

oracle_analysis.table: per setting and averaged over 30-60 dB and the full grid: NMSE of O, A, best single-constant arm, B
oracle_analysis.best_single_constant_arm: the frozen single-constant arm (C1, C2 or D if run) with the lowest full-grid mean-setting test NMSE (reporting only)
oracle_analysis.conclusion_rule: If A - O < 0.3 dB on average (full grid and 30-60 dB) and < 1 dB in every setting, conclude that further filter development is unlikely to pay off

truth_use: True channels only for scoring and the oracle; never for selection of A-D.
storage: Large caches (anchor banks with truth, pre-filter estimates) are kept out of git; their SHA-256 hashes are committed.
